title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + rope/rotary fused ops + continuous KV batching
author: Diego Ramirez
description: Motivation: We need to reduce tail latency and improve GPU utilization for medium-to-long sequence inference workloads without changing model weights. This PR upgrades the attention code-paths to FlashAttentionV2 variants, merges fused rotary/rope operations into the attention kernel where safe, and adds continuous KV batching support in the runtime scheduler. Summary of changes: 1) Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernel selection into the operator dispatch (new flag runtime.attn.flashattn_v2_enabled). 2) Implement fused ops that combine rotary/rope application with q/k/v projections and attention matmul to reduce memory traffic and kernel launches. 3) Add continuous KV batching in the request router and KV cache manager so that long-running streaming sessions amortize KV setup costs across tokens. 4) Extend scheduler policies to prefer fused kernels for sequence lengths > 512 and to fall back to compatibility kernels for edge cases (int8 quantized models, non-contiguous buffers). 5) Add comprehensive tests and microbench harness for kernels and end-to-end perf tests with Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B reference prompts. Implementation notes: - Operator layer now probes device capabilities and chooses among [flashattn_v2_fused_rope, flashattn_v2_fused_rotary, flashattn_v1_compat] based on model config and buffer layout. - Fused ops preserve dtype semantics and include patched kernels for quantized int8 paths (uses existing quantization kernels but with extra reorder step when required). - Continuous KV batching implemented as a configurable policy: runtime.kv.continuous_batching_max_windows (default=8) and adaptive drain thresholds. - Added a canary rollout: runtime flag default off in hosted API; enabled by default in dedicated/staging; gradual rollout via rollout rules in console for 48h. Backwards compatibility: Kernel selection is conservative; models with custom attention implementations or unusual rotary/rope encodings use compatibility paths. No model spec changes required. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for fused kernel correctness (comparing outputs to baseline FlashAttentionV1 implementation across seed space). - End-to-end correctness across rope vs rotary modes verified using the eval harness. - Microbenchmarks show consistent improvements. Metrics collected during canary on a staging shard: median token latency reduced by ~22% for Llama-2-13B decodes at seq_len=1024, p95 reduced by ~28%; throughput improvement of ~18% under 95th percentile load. Rollout & monitoring: - Canary rollout to staging followed by dedicated clusters in us-west-2. - Added new observability metrics: attn.kernel.variant, attn.kernel.latency, attn.fused_op_hit. - Alerts: p95 token latency increase > 10% on canary triggers automatic rollback. Related work: ENG-7421 (kernel upgrade epic), ENG-7503 (kv batching scheduler). See SUP-2312 for customer ticket that motivated long-sequence tail latency fixes. Checklist: [x] kernel integration [x] fused op correctness tests [x] kv continuous batching implementation [x] CI passing [x] canary rollout plan
commits: feat(attn): add FlashAttentionV2 kernel selector and capability probe
perf(attn): implement fused rotary/rope + qkv kernel
test(attn): add fused-kernel unit tests and microbench harness
docs(ops): rollout notes and feature flags
discussion: Initial review found a numerical mismatch in rotary fused path (Maya Lin). Root cause: missing sign-extension when reordering int8 blocks for the quantized path; addressed by reordering helper and added a deterministic slow path test (Elliot Green). Jonah requested a scheduler knob to limit continuous batching windows per-shard; implemented and reviewed. Priya validated observability and suggested an extra tag attn.fused_op_hit=true/false which was added. CI flaked on one Linux build due to CUDA driver mismatch; rerun succeeded. Final approval after perf numbers and canary pass.
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops and continuous KV batching. Expect ~20-30% lower token latency and ~15-20% higher throughput for long-sequence workloads on supported hardware. Ops: feature gated; gradual rollout with canary and observability metrics added.
performance_metrics: staging canary: Llama-2-13B seq=1024 median_token_latency -22%, p95 -28%; throughput +18% under stress. Mistral-7B seq=512 median -18%. Memory transient allocation reduced by ~12%.
test_plan: Run unit tests for fused kernels (tests/attn/fused_kernel_tests.py), microbenchmarks (benchmarks/microbench/attn_flashattnv2.py) on CUDA 12 GPUs and run end-to-end decode tests on Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B in staging. Monitor attn.kernel.latency and attn.fused_op_hit during canary. Rollback if p95 token latency regresses >10%.
rollback_plan: Flip runtime.attn.flashattn_v2_enabled=false and drain canary shard; scheduler will revert to compatibility kernels. Ops to run: rollback flag, redeploy canary config, and mark incident if customer impact observed.
